methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $58M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Verdant Robotics, founded by Gabe Sibley and Curtis Garner, is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $58M to date. The valuation analysis considers a comparable universe of 9 private companies and 1 public entity operating in the same sector and stage proximity, including peers such as Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses the $58M total raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A to next-stage advancement, implying a valuation of $116M. The peer-median method draws from four robotics companies at Series B and Seed stages, which exhibit a median valuation of $1.7B (range: $1.1B–$2.0B). This wider peer set reflects the heterogeneity of valuations across the sector at nearby stages.

The triangulated analysis yields a median implied value of $908M, with a low bound of $99M and a high bound of $2.0B. The substantial spread reflects material uncertainty in stage-appropriate comparability; the stage-progression method conservatively anchors the lower end, while peer valuations—skewed toward later-stage companies—anchor the upper end. The key driver of valuation uncertainty is whether Verdant's growth trajectory and unit economics align more closely with earlier-stage peers or with the more mature Series B cohort. Additional clarity on revenue traction and capital efficiency would refine this range materially.
